standard_prerequisites.name: The objects of D(Ab) are complexes of abelian groups up to homotopy of maps, and a morphism in D(Ab) between two complexes is represented by a morphism of complexes after resolving the source by a complex of projectives
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 23363-23367, where the author appeals to the definition of morphisms in D(Ab) to find a complex and a morphism of complexes representing a prescribed composition
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the transition map of complexes that represents the composite in D(Ab), which is what makes the resulting system a system of complexes rather than a system of derived objects.

standard_prerequisites.name: The category D(Ab(N)) of inverse systems of complexes of abelian groups has as morphisms the levelwise morphisms of complexes, and two such systems are isomorphic when every level is an isomorphism in D(Ab) and the transition maps agree in D(Ab)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 23336-23347, where the object M = (M_n) of D(Ab(N)) and the isomorphisms M_n -> K_n are required
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the exact form of the lifting that has to be constructed level by level.

standard_prerequisites.name: An inverse system indexed by the natural numbers may be constructed by induction on the length of its finite initial segments
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 23351-23355 and closed at proof line 23372
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the levelwise construction into an induction, with the case of length one as the initial step.

core_obligations: Start the induction by choosing a complex M_1 of abelian groups representing K_1 (proof lines 23350-23351).
Assume that complexes M_e -> M_{e-1} -> ... -> M_1 together with maps psi_i : M_i -> K_i have been constructed so that the diagrams commute in D(Ab) for all n less than e (proof lines 23352-23355).

Consider the diagram with M_n at the top and the map K_{n+1} -> K_n at the bottom, and use the definition of morphisms in D(Ab) to find a complex M_{n+1}, an isomorphism M_{n+1} -> K_{n+1} in D(Ab) and a morphism of complexes M_{n+1} -> M_n representing the composite K_{n+1} -> K_n composed with the inverse of psi_n in D(Ab) (proof lines 23356-23371).

Conclude by induction that the inverse system M = (M_n) with its levelwise isomorphisms to the given K_n and its strictly commuting transition diagrams exists, which is the assertion of the lemma (proof lines 23371-23373).
proof_roadmap: Represent K_1 by a complex M_1 of abelian groups and announce an induction on the length of the initial segment of the system (proof lines 23351-23355).

Given the segment up to level e with commuting diagrams in D(Ab), use the definition of morphisms in D(Ab) to produce the next complex M_{n+1} together with the iso to K_{n+1} and the transition map to M_n representing the prescribed composite (proof lines 23356-23371).
Close the induction to obtain the system of complexes with the required commuting diagrams (proof lines 23371-23373).
difficulty_reason: The statement compares an inverse system (K_n) of objects of the derived category D(Ab), which is not the same thing as a system of complexes, with a system of complexes whose transition diagrams commute strictly; it asserts that every such inverse system in D(Ab) can be represented by an object of D(Ab(N)) together with levelwise isomorphisms making the diagrams commute in D(Ab) (statement lines 23334-23348). The proof is an induction on the length of the system in which the nontrivial step is the construction of the next transition map: one has to realize the composite of the given map K_{n+1} -> K_n with the inverse of the chosen isomorphism as an honest morphism of complexes, and this is exactly what the definition of morphisms in D(Ab) provides (proof lines 23356-23371). The diagram is a diagram in D(Ab) and is displayed with Xy-pic in the author's markup. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
